egress.terms: Verbatim matrix: 'Traffic usage is unlimited and free of charge. Please note that our unlimited traffic policy does not apply to servers that have the 10G uplink addon. In this special case, we will charge the usage over 20TB with € 1.00, excl. VAT/ TB.' SX65 has a 1 Gbit port and no 10G option. So for SX65 the unlimited clause is unconditional. Guaranteed bandwidth 1 Gbit/s.

interface_detail: full root: any of S3/MinIO, SFTP, NFS, iSCSI, WebDAV you install
chaining: run MinIO → put Cloudflare in front → signed URLs; or mount as NFS target for an AList/OpenList front-end
limits_note: Single machine, no provider-side redundancy beyond your own RAID. €39 setup fee. IPv4 billed separately at €1.70/mo per the price-adjustment doc.
reliability_note: Provides cost-effective dedicated storage in European datacenters. Hardware administration, disk replacement, and RAID management are user-maintained.
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.

evidence.proved: SX65 from €84.00/mo excl. VAT, 4×16TB up to 4×22TB SATA, 1 GBit/s guaranteed, Traffic Unlimited
SX65-2 = 'AMD Ryzen 7 3700X, 64 GB DDR4 ECC, 4x 16 TB SATA Enterprise HDD'; 10 Gbit NIC explicitly 'not for SX65'
'hetzner SX65 would probably be your best bet, just doesn't have the connection speed but I doubt you would at that price'

price_per_tb_month: €1.29/TB/mo at 64 TB raw (€82.30 ÷ 64) ≈ $1.49. €1.71/TB/mo at 48 TB RAID-5 usable (€82.30 ÷ 48). SX65-1 at 88 TB raw: €272.30 ÷ 88 = €3.09/TB — worse, because the 22 TB config carries NVMe. The 16 TB config is the outlier.
